title: The one who became many
hook: the week's story told whole: the one self becomes all
carry: the one self became all of us
tomorrow: 'I was Manu, and the sun.' a boast, or a fever?

segments.voice: Yesterday, I am, said first by Brahman, beside I AM, God's own name to Moses: whoever wakes to Brahman may say it. Today the week comes back.

Three little words: aham, I; brahma, Brahman; asmi, am. A floormate reads them on a door sign and asks the obvious thing. So you think you're a god? The honest answer is in the story this week has told in pieces. Today it's told whole, start to finish.
screen: `AHAM. BRAHMA. ASMI.` → `SO YOU THINK YOU'RE A GOD?` → `THE WHOLE STORY.`

segments.voice: In the beginning, the Brihadaranyaka says, there was only the self, in the shape of a person. It looked around, saw nothing but itself, and its first word was I am. Then it was afraid, the way anyone alone in the dark is afraid, until it asked: there's nothing here but me, so what am I afraid of? And the fear left, because fear comes from a second. But alone, it had no delight. So it longed for a second, and split itself in two, and from that pair, the text says, people were born, and then every kind of creature in pairs, all the way down to the ants. Then it knew: I am this creation, for I poured it all out of myself. And it entered everything it had become, to the tips of the fingernails, hidden like a razor in its case. It's dearer than anything, because it's innermost. And a few verses on, the text says it plainly: in the beginning this was Brahman, and it knew itself, I am Brahman, and so it became all. Here's the big teaching, plainly. Most Vedanta teachers, Shankara and Ramanuja among them, read this as Brahman being both the maker of the world and what the world is made of. The one became the many, and lives in each one as its self, its atman. That's why, as many teachers read it, aham brahmasmi isn't one person's boast. If it's true of me, it's true of the floormate asking, too.
screen: `THE SELF ALONE: I AM.` · `NO SECOND, SO NO FEAR.` · `IT SPLIT, AND ENTERED ALL.` · `I AM BRAHMAN: IT BECAME ALL.` · then, large: `THE ONE BECAME THE MANY.`

segments.voice: Stand and take a slow walk, across the room and back. On one step think aham, on the next brahma, on the next asmi. On the way back, bring to mind the people nearby, one by one, and let the three words keep time for them too. When you sit again, let them go.
Aham brahmasmi: I am Brahman. Three small words, I, Brahman, am, and the whole story behind them: the one became the many.
Your line: the one self became all of us. That's aham brahmasmi. A full week, well walked.

fork.setup: your little cousin asks: 'if God is in everybody, is God in the mean kid at school too?' by this week's story, what's honest?
options: yes: the one self became everyone, him too, even when he isn't acting like it.
no: only good people have the self inside them.
only priests and sages have Brahman in them.
fork.reveal: in the Brihadaranyaka the one self became all and entered everything to the fingertips, and the saying is opened to gods, sages and people alike.

original.note: Sanskrit brahma, the form of Brahman inside the saying; joined to asmi, it becomes brahmasmi.

trapdoor: what you thought: aham brahmasmi is one person's claim to be a god.

what a scholar hears: Brihadaranyaka 1.4.3–5: the self falls into two and pours out creation ('I am this creation'); Shankara and Ramanuja read Brahman as both the maker and the material of the world (Madhva's school reads it differently).

build the knowing, or see it

sources.ref: Brihadaranyaka Upanishad 1.4.1–8, 1.4.10 (the self alone says 'I am'; fear comes from a second; no delight alone; it falls into two, and from the pair come people and all creatures down to the ants; 'I am this creation, for I poured it forth from myself'; it entered here to the tips of the nails; dearer than all; aham brahmasmi)
Brahma Sutra 1.4.23 (prakritis ca: Brahman is the material cause as well as the maker), as Shankara and Ramanuja read it; Madhva's Dvaita school holds otherwise
